pr_title: Properly calculate binormal when creating SurfaceTool from arrays
pr_body:
Fixes: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/86131

I suspect that this will also fix some other subtle bugs.

This bug has existed in the SurfaceTool code for many many years. But it wasn't caught as there were very few situations where this code made a major impact. However, we started using `create_vertex_array_from_triangle_arrays()` in the default GLTF import path a few years ago. The result was that we ended up forcing the binormal sign of all GLTF meshes to 1.0. This is fine for most meshes, but the binormal sign is necessary when mirroring normal maps, so losing it totally broke those meshes. 

_edit: I have also pushed a related fix that ensures that the binormal sign is properly encoded when sending it to the shader. This fixes a related bug when using the compressed mesh format_

issue_context.title: Mirrored UVs break normal mapping
issue_context.body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.2.1

### System information

Windows 11, Vulkan, Forward+

### Issue description

Having mirrored UVs break normal mapping. I would expect Godot to correctly take mirrored UVs into account like other 3d software does. Not only does it not do that. it creates some very strange normal artifacts in the middle of polygons that I can't explain.

Here is a cube that has been mirrored and had an open gl normal map with a "bump" sphere shape applied to it in Blender:

Model:
![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/4955051/5e7ced96-f22d-4c06-9ae1-0ae4864c8acd)

With mirror modifier:
![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/4955051/d066f922-fa7d-47fe-b78b-edb582846c59)

Normals work as expected:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/4955051/9b4a85bc-8656-4f7d-b9ec-d590dc0e1822

Here the box is imported as gltf into Godot:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/4955051/384aafbb-9760-4a66-968d-9b3bc014ca6c

As you can see the normals are not acting correctly when mirrored and there is for some reaons a strange artifact running down the middle of a polygon where no edge exist.
![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/4955051/919f07b1-2f34-46f2-91a5-75289eacf645)
![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/4955051/f6d0ef5f-56d1-43f0-a6d7-9fddd26ec146)





### Steps to reproduce

Open the MRP and observe the issue.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[mirror_uv_normalmap_issue.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/13665636/mirror_uv_normalmap_issue.zip)
comments:
It looks like you are relying on Godot to generate the tangents with this model. 

Have you tried exporting from blender with tangents included? Blender removes tangents by default. 

The trouble here is that to generate tangents from an existing normal-mapped image, you need to rely on the UVs, but if the UVs behave in an unexpected way, then the thirdparty lib we rely on to generate tangents breaks down. 

When doing normal mapping, you should always use the tangents from your 3DCC instead of relying on Godot to generate them at import time.

So importing the tangents, does make the weird error in the middle of the polygon clear, but the normals are still incorrect.
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/4955051/96e3b8d5-1fbe-4fed-a9b0-a58438ec7971

review_comments: Out of curiosity, where does that `0.500008` come from? It might be worth adding a comment.

Its the smallest number representable by a 16 bit UNORM value in the range 0.5 - 1.0.

Its the flipside of `0.49999` above.
